plan_a_advantages: Includes hill repeats for strength and power development, essential for trail running.
Incorporates tempo runs to improve aerobic threshold and speed.
Includes a dedicated strength training session for injury prevention and performance enhancement.
Offers a more varied training stimulus, reducing the risk of overuse injuries and plateaus.
plan_b_advantages: Emphasizes high volume of easy running, which can be beneficial for building a strong aerobic base.
Simpler structure may be easier to adhere to for some athletes.
The focus on long runs could be advantageous for athletes primarily targeting ultra-distance trail races.
reasoning: While both plans aim to improve trail running speed, Plan A offers a more well-rounded approach to training. It incorporates a variety of session types – long runs, hill repeats, tempo runs, and strength training – which is crucial for developing both aerobic endurance and the specific strength and power needed for trail running. Plan B focuses almost exclusively on long, easy runs, which, while important for base building, may not be sufficient to improve speed and performance on varied terrain. The inclusion of hill repeats and tempo runs in Plan A provides opportunities for targeted improvements in speed and lactate threshold.
